turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I am aware of the extent of his misfortunes, sir. And I am also aware of the cause of them. Your pride and arrogance have been the source of much pain for him and others.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Your words are harsh, Miss Bennet, but they are not unexpected. I have often been guilty of reserve and pride, which have led to misunderstandings and pain. It is a character flaw I have long been aware of and one I strive to correct.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I cannot deny the truth of your words, Mr. Darcy, but actions speak louder than words. Your conduct towards me and my family has been anything but respectful or considerate.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I understand your criticism, Elizabeth. My actions towards you and your family have been the source of much regret. I hope that through time and sincere effort, I may earn your forgiveness and respect.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I have no doubt that you wish to change, Mr. Darcy. But it will take more than words to convince me of your sincerity. Your actions will need to prove your commitment to a better path.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I understand your skepticism, Elizabeth. I shall endeavor to demonstrate my sincerity through my actions, not merely my words. My past conduct is my own fault, and I shall work to rectify it.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I am willing to see the fruits of your labor, Mr. Darcy, but do not expect it to be easy or swift. My trust and respect are not lightly given.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I shall respect your expectations, Elizabeth, and work diligently to earn your trust and respect through my actions alone.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I appreciate your resolve, Mr. Darcy. Let us see where this path leads us both.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I shall do all in my power to earn your trust, Elizabeth. I am committed to this path.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I will observe your efforts closely, Mr. Darcy. Your actions will speak louder than your words.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I understand your caution, Elizabeth. My actions will indeed be the measure of my sincerity.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I shall do the same, Mr. Darcy. Let us both strive to improve.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I shall endeavour to earn your esteem, Elizabeth. Your judgment is one I hold in the highest regard.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I shall hold you to that, Mr. Darcy. Your sincerity will be tested by time and action.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I am resolved to prove myself worthy, Elizabeth. Your opinion means much to me.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I believe you, Mr. Darcy, but my trust must be earned. Prove to me that you have changed.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I shall do all in my power to earn your trust, Elizabeth. My heart is yours to command, should it ever be worthy of it.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Mr. Darcy, I must be frank. My feelings for you are far from what you seek. Prove to me that you can be the man I respect and perhaps, with time, you will earn more than just my esteem.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I understand the depth of your distrust, Elizabeth. I shall work to earn your respect and perhaps one day, your regard.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: In vain have I struggled. It will not do. My feelings will not be repressed. You must allow me to tell you how ardently I admire and love you.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: In such cases as this, it is, I believe, the established mode to express a sense of obligation for the sentiments avowed, however unequally they may be returned. It is natural that obligation should be felt, and if I could feel gratitude, I would now thank you. But I cannot--I have never desired your good opinion, and you have certainly bestowed it most unwillingly. I am sorry to have occasioned pain to anyone. It has been most unconsciously done, however, and I hope will be of short duration. The feelings which you tell me have long prevented the acknowledgment of your regard can have little difficulty in overcoming it after this explanation.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: And this is all the reply which I am to have the honour of expecting! I might, perhaps, wish to be informed why, with so little endeavour at civility, I am thus rejected. But it is of small importance.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: I might as well inquire, why, with so evident a design of offending and insulting me, you chose to tell me that you liked me against your will, against your reason, and even against your character? Was not this some excuse for incivility, if I was uncivil? But I have other provocations. You know I have. Had not my own feelings decided against you, had they been indifferent, or had they even been favourable, do you think that any consideration would tempt me to accept the man who has been the means of ruining, perhaps for ever, the happiness of a most beloved sister?

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: I have every reason in the world to think ill of you. No motive can excuse the unjust and ungenerous part you acted there. You dare not, you cannot deny that you have been the principal, if not the only means of dividing them from each other, of exposing one to the censure of the world for caprice and instability, the other to its derision for disappointed hopes, and involving them both in misery of the acutest kind.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: But it is not merely this affair, on which my dislike is founded. Long before it had taken place, my opinion of you was decided. Your character was unfolded in the recital which I received many months ago from Mr. Wickham. On this subject, what can you have to say? In what imaginary act of friendship can you here defend yourself? or under what misrepresentation can you here impose upon others?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: You take an eager interest in that gentleman’s concerns

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Who that knows what his misfortunes have been can help feeling an interest in him?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: His misfortunes! yes, his misfortunes have been great indeed.
